Fit the assembled blocks to the closest positive semi-definite matrix

Source: R/project_psd.R
indri_project_psd.Rd

The average of overlapping subset estimates is not a covariance matrix: it is a patchwork, and nothing constrains it to be positive semi-definite. This fits the full matrix that is closest to all the subset estimates at once,

Usage

indri_project_psd(
  blocks,
  subsets,
  K = NULL,
  init = NULL,
  weights = c("none", "inverse_variance"),
  control = list()
)

Arguments

blocks

List of subset fits, each with a G matrix and, when weights = "inverse_variance", a se matrix or draws array.

subsets

Integer matrix of trait indices, one subset per row.

K

Number of traits; inferred from subsets when NULL.

init

Starting matrix. Defaults to the average of the blocks.

weights

"none" for LiMMBo's equal weights, or "inverse_variance" to weight each block's entries by their inverse uncertainty.

control

Optional list of controls for stats::optim().

Value

A list with matrix, the fitted PSD matrix, plus convergence, value and the raw optim result.

Details

C* = argmin over C >= 0 of sum_j || W_j * (C[I_j, I_j] - G_j) ||_F^2

by writing C = L L' with L lower triangular, which makes every candidate positive semi-definite by construction, and optimising the K (K + 1) / 2 free entries of L with L-BFGS-B. The average is used as the starting point. The per-entry weights W_j are all one unless weights = "inverse_variance", in which case they come from each block's se or draws (see indri_assemble()).

Examples

# Three pairwise estimates can imply an indefinite full matrix.
subsets <- t(utils::combn(3, 2))
blocks <- list(
  list(G = matrix(c(1, 0.9, 0.9, 1), 2)),
  list(G = matrix(c(1, -0.9, -0.9, 1), 2)),
  list(G = matrix(c(1, 0.9, 0.9, 1), 2))
)
average <- indri_assemble(blocks, subsets)$G
eigen(average, symmetric = TRUE)$values
#> [1]  1.9  1.9 -0.8
fit <- indri_project_psd(blocks, subsets)
fit$matrix
#>            [,1]      [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,]  1.1599995 0.5799982 -0.5799998
#> [2,]  0.5799982 1.1599979  0.5800003
#> [3,] -0.5799998 0.5800003  1.1599990
fit$convergence
#> [1] 0
eigen(fit$matrix, symmetric = TRUE)$values
#> [1] 1.740000e+00 1.739997e+00 7.683854e-12
